# Results — Study 523 (Investment-To-Assets) on the real survivor basket

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: investment-to-assets
IA = CapEx_t / Total_Assets_{t-1}, from SEC EDGAR companyfacts
(`PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment`, `Assets`). Forward returns from Yahoo
daily adjusted prices. As-of **2026-06-27**.*

**Definition**:
- IA_t = |CapEx_t| / Total_Assets_{t-1}  (higher = heavier investor)

**Prediction (Titman-Wei-Xie 2004 / Fama-French CMA)**: HIGH IA → LOW future returns.
We go **long low-IA / short high-IA** (g1 − g3).

**Execution lag (one)**: IA from fiscal year y drives a 12-month forward total return that
*begins 4 months after the fiscal-year-end* (when the 10-K is public) and is entered at
the close 1 trading day later. A forward window is used only if it has fully completed by
the as-of date — no partial period is ever stamped.

**Universe**: a fixed ~40-name large-cap **survivor** basket; ~27 names/year carry the
EDGAR capex tag. **Survivorship-biased** — every firm survived to 2026.

**Window**: 16 signal years (2009–2024), forecasting 12-month returns 2010–2026.

## Synthetic positive control (seed-robust, 25 seeds)

| Planted premium | Mean hedge | Mean HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00/yr (null) | −0.1%/yr | −0.15 |
| −0.06/yr | +13.0%/yr | +14.94 |
| −0.10/yr | +21.8%/yr | +25.00 |

The engine recovers a planted investment effect with a large, seed-robust t-stat, and the
null behaves (t ≈ 0). The real-tape null is therefore a statement about the **market and
the survivor basket**, not the method.

## Verdict

The predicted effect (high capital-investment → low returns) is **absent** on this survivor
basket. The long-low-IA / short-high-IA hedge earns **+0.04%/yr** with HAC *t* = **+0.01** —
indistinguishable from zero. The placebo p = **0.471** (the real result is buried inside the
label-shuffle null), the low-IA leg beats only **55%** of random same-size draws (chance),
and the gross edge of essentially zero turns to **−0.66%/yr net** once costs and short
borrow are charged. The low and high IA terciles earn near-identical returns (+19.4% each).

The synthetic control proves the engine is faithful: planting a −6%/yr investment effect
yields HAC *t* ≈ +15 (seed-robust over 25 seeds), and the null behaves (*t* ≈ 0). So the
absence on the real tape is a property of the market and the basket, not the method.

Two honest reasons the academic anomaly does not appear here:

1. **Wrong universe.** Titman-Wei-Xie (2004) and the CMA factor are estimated on the broad
   cross-section of all US stocks, dominated by small and mid-caps where over-investment and
   limits-to-arbitrage bite hardest. On ~27 heavily-covered large caps the effect is thin
   and arbitraged.
2. **Survivorship selection.** The high-IA group on a survivor basket includes successful
   capex-heavy expanders (semiconductor fabs, hyperscale datacentres, energy majors) whose
   investment was productive — the opposite of the over-investing failures the anomaly was
   built around (note 2024: high-IA +76% as the AI-datacentre capex names ripped).

- **Signal — NONE** (hedge *t* = +0.01; placebo p = 0.47; beats 55% of random draws;
  literature supports the effect for a broad non-biased universe, not survivor large-caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (no gross edge; −0.66%/yr net after costs and borrow; nothing to
  trade).
- **Capex vs total-asset-growth channel — BUSTED** (the capex/PP&E investment channel is no
  more present than the total-asset-growth channel in [Study 244](../../244-asset-growth/);
  both vanish on the survivor large-cap panel).
